name: Token Receiver (beacons)
description: Callback endpoint for beacons (DNS tokens, web bugs, kubeconfig files) created on the Hub's Beacons page. Deploy it on its own internet-facing node; the Hub stays internal.

documentation.summary: The Token Receiver is an authoritative-only DNS server for one delegated zone and a fixed-response HTTP endpoint. Beacons the Hub generates point into that zone. When an intruder uses one (resolves the planted host name, opens a document with a web bug, runs kubectl with the planted kubeconfig) the lookup or request reaches the receiver, which raises a critical beacon_triggered event. Tokens are HMAC-tagged, so random names under the zone raise nothing.

sections.title: Features
content: DNS (UDP and TCP): answers SOA/NS at the apex and A for every name in the zone (TS_ANSWER_IPV4); everything else is NODATA. Names outside the zone are REFUSED: no recursion, no forwarding.
Records the resolver, query name and type, and the EDNS Client Subnet when the resolver sends one (the network of the real client behind a public resolver).

HTTP: every request gets the same 1x1 GIF with no-cache headers; requests carrying a token are recorded with method, host, path, User-Agent and Referer. X-Forwarded-For is believed only from TS_TRUSTED_PROXIES.
One event per token and channel per TS_ALERT_COOLDOWN; repeats are counted (repeats_since_last).

sections.title: Deployment
content: Delegate a subdomain (e.g. t.example.com) to this host: NS record for the subdomain pointing at a name with an A record (glue) for the receiver's public address.
Expose udp+tcp/53 and tcp/80 from the internet to this node only. The node needs outbound HTTPS to the Hub's sensor API and nothing else.
For HTTPS web bugs, terminate TLS on a front end (F5) and list it in TS_TRUSTED_PROXIES.

sections.title: Security Architecture
content: Global Sandbox Baseline: Enforced by the TrueSignal Hub. Drops ALL default Linux kernel capabilities and enforces a read-only filesystem.
Execution Privilege: Runs as container root (UID 0) strictly to bind ports 53 and 80.
Token check: TS_BEACON_KEY is a Hub-derived key shared by all receivers; the master never leaves the Hub. It can verify tokens but the Hub decides which beacon a token belongs to.
DNS replies are rate-limited per source (50/s) and no larger than a few records, so spoofed queries can't use the receiver as an amplifier.

heuristics.recommendation_reason: Deploy manually on an internet-facing node to receive beacon callbacks.

env_vars.name: TS_HUB_ENDPOINT
env_vars.description: The URL of your central TrueSignal Hub.

env_vars.name: TS_SENSOR_ID
env_vars.description: Unique identifier for this specific trap.

env_vars.name: TS_SEVERITY
env_vars.description: Unused: beacon events are always critical; the Hub lowers unknown tokens to medium.

env_vars.name: TS_BEACON_DOMAIN
env_vars.description: The zone delegated to this receiver, e.g. t.example.com. Beacons created on the Hub point into it.

env_vars.name: TS_BEACON_NS
env_vars.description: Comma-separated name servers of the zone, as in the parent's NS records. Default ns1.<zone>.

env_vars.name: TS_ANSWER_IPV4
env_vars.description: This receiver's public IPv4 address. A queries for the zone are answered with it, so web bugs reach the HTTP listener. Empty: A queries get NODATA (DNS beacons still fire).

env_vars.name: TS_SERVICES
env_vars.description: Comma-separated listeners as proto:port (dns serves UDP and TCP).

env_vars.name: TS_ALERT_COOLDOWN
env_vars.description: Minimum time between two events for the same token and channel (one lookup is several queries).

env_vars.name: TS_TRUSTED_PROXIES
env_vars.description: IPs/CIDRs of a TLS front end whose X-Forwarded-For is believed. Empty: the TCP peer is the source.

env_vars.name: TS_BEACON_KEY
env_vars.description: Set by the Hub: the receiver key that verifies beacon tokens. Any value set here is ignored.
